walkthrough: Recall the accepted acceleration of free fall on Earth is about $9.81$ $\text{m s}^{-2}$, so compare the quoted central value $10$ $\text{m s}^{-2}$ with this.
The quoted interval is $10 - 2 = 8$ $\text{m s}^{-2}$ to $10 + 2 = 12$ $\text{m s}^{-2}$, which clearly contains $9.81$ $\text{m s}^{-2}$, so the value agrees with the true value and is accurate.
Precision is shown by the size of the uncertainty: $\pm 2$ $\text{m s}^{-2}$ on $10$ $\text{m s}^{-2}$ is $(2/10) \times 100$% $= 20$%, a very large spread.
A $20$% uncertainty means the result is not sharply defined, so it is not precise despite being accurate.
Accurate but not precise matches the description. This is option A.
